ai.title: Add .agents/types scaffolding and Zod schema error handling
ai.summary: CLI init command now scaffolds .agents/types directory with agent-definition, tools, and util-types files. Agent runtime adds ensureJsonSchemaCompatible helper to catch Zod-to-JSON-Schema conversion failures, falling back to passthrough objects. Scope covers cli/src/commands/init.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/prompts.ts plus templates/prompts.ts. Schema errors in lookup-agent-info.ts return { type: 'object', description: 'Schema unavailable' } instead of throwing.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant setup command, it now creates a ready-made folder at.agents/types with starter template files for defining agents, tools, and shared types, so you don't have to write those from scratch. At the same time, if the assistant runs into a tool whose input format can't be safely converted into a shareable schema, it no longer crashes; instead it skips that tool's schema and continues working with the rest. You'd notice this if you just set up a new assistant project and opened the.agents/types directory, or if your project includes custom tools that previously caused setup or runtime errors due to schema conversion problems.

ai.title: Fix TypeScript compatibility in CLI init and agent schema handling
ai.summary: Added `@ts-expect-error` comments to suppress TypeScript errors for Bun-specific `with { type: 'text' }` import attributes in `cli/src/commands/init.ts`. This resolves compatibility issues where the standard TypeScript compiler rejects Bun's text import syntax. Scope limited to CLI init command and agent runtime schema tests.

eli5.text: When setting up a new project, the tool reads some template files into memory all at once. The code that reads those files uses a syntax that one popular checker doesn't understand, so the checker was flagging it as a mistake. The setup now quietly tells that checker to skip just those few lines. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you're watching the checker's output directly.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.553 released
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.553 in cli/release/package.json (package name "codebuff"). This is a release-bump commit within the same-day sequence that adds /help command and project picker screen, introduces .agents/types scaffolding with Zod schema error handling, and ships ban-conditions, Stripe metering, and store agent dependency tree features. The bump itself is the only file-level change.
ai.evidence: Diff modifies cli/release/package.json: "version" changed from "1.0.552" to "1.0.553". Commit metadata category is CLI, nature release-bump. Package name in manifest is "codebuff".

eli5.text: The Freebuff CLI 1.0.553 release improves your experience with better documentation navigation, smarter help features, and stronger account protections. Mobile users can now tap anywhere on the docs navigation bar to open menus, and a new /help command plus a project picker screen make it easier to get started or switch contexts without fumbling with settings. The documentation sidebar is now simpler, showing a flat list of topics instead of grouped sections, and tables and diagrams render more reliably across devices. A new automatic ban system protects the service by suspending accounts that file too many disputed charges through Stripe, and the dependency tree visualization lets you see how built-in agents relate to each other at a glance. Upgrading gives you smoother in-app navigation, clearer help content, and a more stable, trustworthy environment where abusive activity is filtered out automatically.
